subject: Renewal request: Dedicated pool expansion + surge-smoothing autoscale policy
messages:
From: Kate Liu <kate.liu@acmeai.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmeai.com
Date: 2027-05-30T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal: Dedicated pool + autoscale adjustments

Hi Aisha,

We’re approaching our annual renewal and need to align on capacity and autoscaling behavior for our dedicated pool. Over the last 6 months we saw peak inference load where concurrency spiked to ~320 QPS (latency-sensitive features) and sustained levels around 180–220 QPS. To avoid degradation during product events we’re planning to reserve additional GPUs and want tighter guarantees on scale-up behavior.

Specifically we’re evaluating the following as part of the renewal:
- Add 12 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs to our existing pool (effective at renewal date).
- Minimum warm pool floor of 6 pre-warmed replicas to cut cold-starts.
- Max replicas cap at 30 during bursts.
- Scale-up lag budget: target <= 25s for reaching additional replicas from the warm pool; if exceeded, automatic fallback to a smaller low-latency model.
- Throughput guarantee: a committed throughput percentile (p95) during business hours; we’re open on exact wording but want credits if throughput drops below threshold.

Can you outline what terms and pricing changes this would imply, and whether Redwood can provide a short mutual action plan so we can get legal/procurement moving? Also any notes on how warm pool billing works would be helpful — do we pay full reserved cost for warm replicas?

Thanks,
Kate
Kate Liu
Head of Platform, Acme AI

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>

Cc: procurement@acmeai.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com

Hi Kate — thanks for the clear ask and the numbers. We can accommodate the expansion and propose the following starting point so procurement/legal have something concrete to review:

- Reserved capacity: +12 GPUs added to your Dedicated pool, billed as reserved units on renewal. We’ll show both monthly amortized and upfront commit options in the term sheet (attached: redwood-dedicated-term-sheet-v2.pdf).
- Warm pool: minimum of 6 pre-warmed replicas. Warm replicas are billed at a discounted reserved rate (we charge a warm-pool reservation fee rather than full active pricing) — see warmpool-capacity-model.xlsx for the cost delta.
- Autoscaling policy: min_replicas = 4 (non-evictable), warm_pool_floor = 6 (pre-warmed standby), max_replicas = 30. We recommend a two-stage scale-up: first expand from warm pool (fast, nominal lag), then spin new replicas to reach burst target.
- Scale-up lag SLA: propose contractual target of 30s to reach additional capacity from warm pool for 90% of scale events, with engineering SLO at 25s. We can include a credit schedule if p95 lag exceeds 45s.
- Throughput/availability: propose a committed throughput band during business hours with SLA credits tied to p95 throughput shortfalls. Exact thresholds we can align on in next call.

Next steps:
1) Technical sync with your infra team this week to validate the scale-up flow and request telemetry needed for monitoring.
2) Commercial confirmation (pricing table + DocuSign link) once we align on warm-pool billing and scale SLA.
3) Legal review of the term-sheet; we’ll accept redlines on the SLA wording.

I’ve cc’d Marissa (account lead) and will loop in Karthik for implementation details. I’ll attach a short autoscale SLA draft and the capacity model. If that works I can schedule a technical call for Thursday.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Aisha — quick read of the cost model and a first-pass commercial position:

Options (commercial):
- Option A (Commit-heavy): 12 GPUs added as reserved with a 12-month commit, 18% discount on reserved rate, warm-pool fee = 25% of reserved unit price. Best cost predictability.
- Option B (Hybrid): 6 GPUs reserved, 6 GPUs on a burst/credit model for the first 6 months; warm-pool fee 35% while burst credits apply. Good for ramp.
- Option C (Conservative): No new reserve; provide increased soft-cap with higher burst pricing + 4 warm replicas on us for 60 days to prove value.

SLA credit suggestion (starter):
- If p95 scale-up lag > 45s in any monthly measurement window: 5% monthly credit on Dedicated portion; if > 60s: 12% credit. Add clause excluding major incidents and customer misconfiguration.

Warm-pool billing note: agree that charging a warm-pool reservation fee is the simplest. Customers typically want to know if warm replicas are counted toward commit — recommend we count them toward the reserved commit for clarity.

I’ll drop a short pricing table by EOD with numbers for A/B/C. For legal, suggest we keep SLA targets defined by measurable telemetry (p95/p99 lag, warm-pool hit-rate) and include a joint runbook for escalations.

—Marissa
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-06-02T14:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal: Dedicated pool + autoscale adjustments — engineering notes

Folks — technical notes on feasibility and a proposed implementation pattern:

1) Two-stage scale-up (we already have the primitives):
   - Stage 1: Warm pool drain — warm replicas are standby with warmed KV caches; moving requests to warm replicas is fast (~5–12s depending on model size and tokenization).
   - Stage 2: Cold spin-up — additional replicas are created and load-balanced; cold spin is variable (30–90s) depending on model size and instance type.

2) Scale-up lag measurement: we'll instrument the metric "scale_up_time_to_target_replicas" (ms) and expose p50/p95/p99 via the Console. For contract language use p95.

3) Predictive warmup: we can implement a short-term traffic predictor to proactively grow the warm pool ahead of predictable events (cron-based product events). This reduces reliance on cold spin-up and can push observed lag into the <20s range for most events.

4) Billing: warm replicas counted against reserved commit and charged at warm rate if within committed GPU units; otherwise billed as warm-reservation on top of commit. Need the final commercial decision on whether warm replicas count toward commit.

5) Risk/operational notes: KV cache rehydration for large LMs can add ~3–10s; network provisioning and local NVMe staging (for quantized model) adds variability. Recommend 30s contractual target and an engineering SLO of 22–25s with predictive warmup enabled for major traffic windows.

I’ll prepare a short tech appendix for the SLA (model size buckets, expected warm-time ranges) after Marissa confirms pricing direction.

—Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
